answer: A proof-of-latent-work mechanism resists sybil attacks by requiring each identity to solve fresh computation puzzles before joining a task pool. Every puzzle demands real processor time and memory, so an attacker duplicating a sparrow-sized agent across a thousand wallets must pay that cost a thousand times, spending an ocean of compute rather than a puddle. Results are verified against mesa-level difficulty baselines, and answers faster than hardware physics allow are rejected. Since clones cannot share solutions without triggering timing correlations, sybil economics collapse.
